title: Provide a practical guide for the preferred project stack
goal: Give architecture planning a reusable, source-backed guide for projects that fit the harness's preferred stack.
in_scope: Create a discoverable project-local skill under .agents/skills/ for planning projects with the preferred stack.
Create supporting reference material covering TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Prisma ORM, and pnpm: each technology's role, fit, and relevant alternatives.
Describe a practical frontend/backend starter architecture, how the technologies work together, and an incremental project setup and implementation sequence.
Document material compatibility considerations, common pitfalls, and decision points without presenting changeable versions or support details as timeless facts.
Include official documentation sources and a last-verified date in the reference material; direct the skill to recheck current compatibility, lifecycle, and setup details during project planning.
Update the architecture-planning skill to consult the preferred-stack guide when relevant while treating its choices as defaults that can be overridden by project needs.
out_of_scope: Mandating the preferred stack for every project.
Implementing an application, generating project code, or installing/configuring dependencies in a product repository.
Guaranteeing specific current versions, compatibility combinations, deployment prices, or support lifecycles without rechecking official sources at planning time.
Replacing project-specific requirements discovery or architecture decisions with the reference guide.
acceptance_criteria: The new skill has valid frontmatter and is discoverable under .agents/skills/.
Supporting reference material covers the role and fit of all six preferred technologies and explains their boundaries and relevant alternatives.

The guide includes a coherent starter architecture and an ordered practical setup/implementation path, including important integration points between frontend, backend, database, ORM, and package manager.
Compatibility notes and pitfalls are explicit, and time-sensitive claims have official sources and a last-verified date.
The skill instructs agents to revalidate changeable details from current official sources and not treat the preferred stack as mandatory.
The architecture-planning skill points to and uses the guide when relevant, while retaining project-specific requirements analysis.
